title: Refuse incomplete note identity scans before autosave
description: Reviewing brwr-ezb found that historical note recovery treats Vault::note_candidates' truncated or skipped files as a complete identity source. If a conflicting artifact note sorts beyond the 4096-file or 16 MiB scan cap, an apparently unique candidate can redirect a save. Optional older-note discovery may remain best effort; primary historical key selection must refuse an incomplete scan.
acceptance_criteria: Reproduce a partial scan choosing a note despite omitted candidates; return correlated unavailable identity errors for loads and saves when the primary scan hits a bound or read failure, preserve all existing notes, and keep ordinary optional older-note discovery usable.
close_reason: Preserved shared and older note access across revisioned policy removal, narrowing and cache rebuilds; refused incomplete identity scans before autosave. Fresh complete diff reviewed; 332 Rust tests, 8 extension test files and full required gate green. Commit subject: fix: preserve notes after capture policy removal (SHA assigned by the driver).

title: Recover missing index ingestion from durable logs
description: Reproduced in the 2026-10-18 review against the built host. Deliver activity A, retain its valid index-state.json, deliver durable activity B, restore the earlier cache to simulate an append followed by interrupted or failed index publication, and deliver C. Recent still omits B; explicit brauser reindex restores it. load_or_rebuild only checks cache shape and folder identity, and record_events never checks a log ingestion checkpoint. native.rs reports index update failures only on stderr and acknowledges the durable capture. See DESIGN.md section 12.3.
acceptance_criteria: Add a failing append-versus-index fault regression. A valid but incomplete cache must catch up automatically on the next delivery or query, including after restart and without replay of B. Keep durable log acknowledgement independent of cache success, event-ID idempotence, bounded ingestion work and configuration/write locking. If repair cannot complete, expose stale/unavailable derived history rather than silently presenting it as complete.
notes: Reproduced the reported missing-B history with a failing native regression. Added version-2 per-file length/mtime checkpoints checked before index use; changed logs reparse completely, unchanged logs are skipped, and SQLite publishes before the checkpoint cache. Native note load/view now share the config/write lock because reads can repair the cache. Four new tests cover restart + query/delivery catch-up through single and batch capture, real cache-publication failure, unavailable history responses, duplicate replay, checkpoint migration, partial markers, dirty tracking and bounded aggregate reads. All required checks pass: 326 Rust tests and 8 extension files, both Clippy configurations. macOS smoke runner refuses Linux; dialog count unchanged at 14. Whole-history snapshots and hard cache/read limits remain provisional until brwr-b2e. Commit pending driver if .git is read-only; message in .bosun_commit_msg.
close_reason: Recover durable log entries automatically via bounded per-file ingestion checkpoints, with explicit unavailable history on repair failure; 326 Rust tests and 8 extension files green. Cycle commit pending driver, based on e5a6bb2; message in .bosun_commit_msg.

title: Keep artifact notes reachable after adapter or site removal
description: Reproduced in the 2026-10-18 review against the built native host with an isolated synthetic config and notes folder. Save a note on a recognized URL, remove its adapter through revisioned update_config, then load the same URL. note_context now derives a URL key, and older_notes returns no entries for URL primary keys, so the panel reports no note although the artifact-keyed file remains intact. See host/src/native.rs note_context and host/src/note.rs older_notes; DESIGN.md sections 6.2 and 12.3. A removed site can also retire its adapters. Capturing must stay disabled for removed policy while existing notes remain reachable.
acceptance_criteria: Add a failing native-message regression for save/remove/load, then preserve access to the existing artifact note after adapter removal, recognition narrowing and site removal. Cover alternate known routes, an already occupied URL note, ambiguous historical mappings and cache deletion/reindex. No automatic merge, overwrite or capture re-enable; stale expected_key still refuses a save and preserves copy-out text.
notes: After brwr-ee5, history reads catch up and may publish caches; note load/view now take the config/write lock too. During this bead's full removal matrix, examine note_context's existing best-effort index errors: an unavailable history lookup must not be mistaken for an unambiguous empty mapping and redirect a save. No removal acceptance is claimed by ee5.
close_reason: Shared and older notes remain reachable after revisioned adapter/site removal and recognition narrowing, with alternate routes, occupancy, ambiguity, cache deletion and reindex verified; full gate passes 332 Rust tests and 8 extension test files. Fresh full diff reviewed. Commit: fix: preserve notes after capture policy removal (driver assigns SHA).

title: Make single activity delivery reuse the batch policy check
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

The activity authorization checks exist twice: `record_activity` (host/src/native.rs ~640–717) and `check_activity_policy` (host/src/native.rs ~977–1020). They agree today, but a future fix to one (for example the trail-transition and format-character fixes) can silently miss the other and re-open a worker-trust gap on one delivery path. Make `record_activity` call `check_activity_policy`, and add a test that feeds the same hostile event through both paths and expects identical outcomes. Take this after the other two 2026-10-16 security-review items (ordering, not a block). The wider delivery-path dedupe stays in P3 brwr-o1l.

From the 2026-10-16 security review (read-only, host code at main c908fc5; nothing serious, these are hardening items), not separately verified: confirm with a failing test before fixing. Line numbers are from c908fc5; re-check after step 6.6.
acceptance_criteria: A regression test reproducing the reported gap fails before the fix and passes after; the full Rust and extension suites are green. If the test shows the finding is wrong, close as not reproduced with the reason.
notes: Confirmed duplicate source checks. No behavioral divergence reproduced: the new 13-scenario parity test passed before and after consolidation. record_activity now calls check_activity_policy under its existing config lock. Explicit outcomes, reasons, event correlation, refused-write absence, and decoded accepted payloads are checked across 26 deliveries. Full required gate green: 322 Rust tests and 8 extension files; both Clippy modes. Initial test-only failures assumed plain event IDs/JSON field order and were corrected to decode markers. Wider dedupe remains brwr-o1l. Cycle commit delegated to driver if .git is read-only.
close_reason: Not reproduced as a current behavioral gap: 13-case baseline parity already passed. Confirmed duplication and shipped the requested shared activity authorization plus parity coverage; 322 Rust tests and 8 extension files green. Cycle commit pending driver, based on 8c0b273; message in .bosun_commit_msg.

title: Strip Unicode format characters from logged page text
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

`safe_markdown_line` replaces control characters but lets Unicode format characters through. A page title containing U+202E (RTL override), U+200B–U+200F, U+2066–U+2069, or U+FEFF reaches the daily log and can make one entry look like another (for example, a reversed URL-like title). Obsidian syntax such as `%%`, `==`, and `#tag` also passes. This pre-dates the overnight work (M1). Strip or replace Unicode category Cf in row text (titles and any presentation text), keeping the hex marker payload byte-exact. Also decide whether to neutralize `%%` comments and `#` tags in titles.

From the 2026-10-16 security review (read-only, host code at main c908fc5; nothing serious, these are hardening items), not separately verified: confirm with a failing test before fixing. Line numbers are from c908fc5; re-check after step 6.6.

Step 6.6 added a second renderer, `index.rs::safe_markdown` (~1007 at f517b7a), for artifact files. It has the same gap. Cover both paths, ideally with one shared sanitizer used by the log row writer and the artifact renderer, so they cannot drift (they already differ: index escapes `!`, capture does not). The regression test should feed a hostile title through both the daily log and a regenerated artifact file.
acceptance_criteria: A regression test reproducing the reported gap fails before the fix and passes after; the full Rust and extension suites are green. If the test shows the finding is wrong, close as not reproduced with the reason.
close_reason: Shared presentation sanitizer protects daily rows, regenerated artifact text and worklogs; 319 Rust tests and 8 extension suites green after failing-first regressions and complete review. Cycle commit is supplied by the driver when the workspace Git metadata is read-only.

title: Restrict trail transitions to Chrome's known values
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

`trail.transition` in delivered activity events is accepted as free text up to 64 characters (host/src/capture.rs ~136, activity shape check). Today it is stored only inside the hex marker payload, but the step 6.6 index reader will read it, so an unvalidated worker-supplied string becomes index input. Reject (terminal `rejected`, not retryable) any transition outside Chrome's webNavigation TransitionType set: link, typed, auto_bookmark, auto_subframe, manual_subframe, generated, start_page, form_submit, reload, keyword, keyword_generated. Also allow whatever qualifier encoding the worker already uses, and make the 6.6 reader tolerate older entries.

Full required checks green: 314 Rust tests and 8 extension suites. Cycle commit pending the driver, based on 9de7507; message in .bosun_commit_msg.

title: Use incremental SQLite storage for artifact history
description: The M1.5a index is currently an entire-history JSON event map plus a hand-written SQLite file encoder. Every delivery serializes the map and regenerates the database, and card/Recent/worklog queries deserialize and derive all events instead of reading index.db. MAX_STATE_BYTES imposes a 64 MiB lifetime cache ceiling. Replace this interim design before M3 FTS or claiming readiness for long-lived history; see DESIGN.md sections 6.7 and 12.3.
acceptance_criteria: Use a maintained SQLite engine for transactional incremental ingestion and indexed artifact, Recent and date-range worklog queries, retaining append-only owned log markers as authority. Rebuild old disposable caches without changing log or note identities. Audit any Rust dependency with cargo deny. Demonstrate correctness and bounded query/update costs on representative month/year history fixtures; maintain recovery across append/index interruption, concurrent hosts, root changes and cache deletion.
close_reason: Duplicate of main branch task brwr-b2e, discovered while reconciling six main-only planning commits. Preserve brwr-b2e and its dependency/concurrency tasks as canonical.

Include updates after background delivery and closing during debounce or an in-flight save; preserve pending edits if the browser exposes the current best-effort flush limitation. Keep clipboard and browser effects confined to the disposable profile.

Close/reopen cases cover a pending debounce and edits made during an in-flight save; any lost edits receive durable recovery before acceptance. Existing setup smoke and dialog counts remain correct.

title: Replace the hand-written SQLite snapshot with an incremental real-SQLite index
description: Step 6.6 (host/src/index.rs) emits index.db with a custom SQLite file-format writer (build_sqlite) and keeps the real cache in index-state.json. Every publish re-derives all artifacts from the full event history, serializes the whole-history JSON state (64 MiB cap, after which index updates fail), and rewrites the entire index.db. Both are whole-file atomic replacements, so concurrent host processes are last-writer-wins. The writer supports no secondary indexes or overflow records, so M3 FTS5 cannot be built on it. Move to rusqlite with incremental upserts inside transactions (WAL, busy timeout), keep the daily log authoritative and brauser reindex as the full rebuild, and drop the hand-written writer and the whole-history JSON cache. Keep the existing 6.6 tests (hostile title, case-colliding ID, external edit replaced, heavy-use day with no file write, rollup bounds) passing.
acceptance_criteria: index.db is written through rusqlite with per-delivery incremental updates (no full re-derive or full-file rewrite on a normal delivery); a year-scale fixture stays within bounded per-delivery time and has no 64 MiB ceiling; build_sqlite and the whole-history JSON state are removed or reduced to a bounded watermark; brauser reindex reproduces the same tables; all step 6.6 tests and full suites green.
notes:
2026-10-18 review: native views also read and derive the entire JSON event map rather than querying index.db. The replacement must use indexed card/Recent/worklog queries and representative month/year fixtures, and retain automatic catch-up from authoritative log checkpoints (brwr-ee5). Current native writes already use the configuration lock; preserve that protection while adding SQLite transaction/WAL/busy-timeout semantics.
brwr-ee5 adds format-2 per-file length/mtime ingestion checkpoints and a 64 MiB aggregate changed-log read cap (32 MiB/file), returning unavailable history without partial publication when a pass cannot complete. Real SQLite ingestion should resume bounded batches across requests so cache rebuilds larger than one pass can progress; preserve the source-log recovery, durable-ack independence and stale-history regressions. This is the existing scaling task, not a second SQLite implementation.

title: Re-learn a site's capture with automatic re-keying of existing records
description: Machine-drafted adapters will sometimes choose the wrong artifact ID, and users who never see the adapter cannot hand-edit it. Today an adapter's ID template is frozen until alias migrations exist (adapter_id_history). title: Preserve single-event recovery across presentation changes
description: Discovered while reviewing brwr-1fo: VisitIntent v1 stores only the hash of the rendered entry. After an upgrade changes escaping or Unicode filtering, a legacy single-event intent whose marker was not completed compares the new rendered bytes with the old hash and returns retryable/manual repair. Complete markers still deduplicate; compact batch intents retain their exact prepared bytes. This is fail-closed and preserves the log, but the queued legacy visit cannot finish automatically. Give single-event recovery a bounded representation independent of future renderer revisions, with an explicit safe recovery path for older intents; never guess at or overwrite an edited log.
acceptance_criteria: A regression starts with pre-upgrade legacy intent/hash and torn bytes, then retries under a changed renderer without losing the event, duplicating a complete marker, or changing unrelated log bytes. Altered logs, changed selected roots and mismatched payloads remain refused. Cover legacy records drained through both single and batch delivery. Keep any persisted prepared bytes bounded and host-owned.
notes: Independent review repaired the concrete sanitizer-upgrade regression using the frozen prior rendering only after an exact durable-hash and partial-byte match, through single and batch delivery. Two regressions cover changed payloads, edited tails, complete-marker deduplication, activity and why payloads. This task remains open for a bounded renderer-independent representation for future upgrades.

Native-query tests cover validated edge types, limits and unknown legacy values, and composed panel tests cover opening a source using local fixtures.
